implementation_log.summary: pydantic-settings config loaded from TOML (config/sbr.toml, SBR_CONFIG override) with SBR_<SECTION>__<KEY> environment overrides that are validated. Enforced: read-only source roots (read_only=false rejected); no overlap between sources and var/curation/vault; protected paths (D:\studium_duplicated) can be neither a source root nor a writable root; 'restricted' is rejected for every model role; unknown keys and relative paths rejected; every validation problem listed with its location. The vault stays unset (Q-B02) and role primaries stay unset (Q-B04). Stable config_hash for the run ledger.

SourceFS is the only source-access module: stat, iter_dir (never follows links, reports junctions and reparse points, records per-entry errors without paths), open_binary and read_bytes (os.open with O_RDONLY|O_BINARY|O_NOINHERIT; the returned object refuses writes). (root_id, relpath) addressing refuses '..', drive or absolute components, NUL and ':' (ADS). Extended-length \\?\ paths handle long names and trailing dots or spaces. The real path must stay inside the root and outside protected paths (junction escapes refused). Original display path kept for provenance. SourceWriteGuard (runtime) patches os/shutil/open/io.open/os.open mutators and refuses and records any target under source or protected roots. assert_writable() is the check for all future writers. The static AST scan has a reviewed allow-list (sourcefs.py, safety.py).

implementation_log.summary: registry.sqlite in var/db (path checked against protected roots before anything is created). Connections use WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON and a busy timeout, in autocommit mode with explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions (single-writer discipline). Numbered migrations (migrations/registry/NNNN_name.sql plus .down.sql) with contiguity checks. schema_version stores SHA-256 checksums over CRLF-normalized text, so edited or unknown applied migrations are refused. Each migration applies in one transaction with foreign_key_check before COMMIT and rolls back on failure. The SQLite online-backup copy goes to var/backups/registry before any change to an existing DB; downgrades are supported. 0001_registry: STRICT tables for activity plus all docs/31 tables, CHECK constraints mirroring the model invariants, FKs from every derived row to activity, and a partial unique index (one present observation per path). Generic typed Repository (insert, upsert, get, find, count; no delete) that validates on write and on read and checks that model fields exist as columns.
implementation_log.verification: TS-MIG: fresh to head; every N-1 (1..head) to head with a synthetic next migration (data retained; backup exists and holds version N-1 with data); failing and FK-violating migrations roll back to N-1; downgrade to 0 and re-upgrade; tamper, CRLF and newer-DB checks. Repository round-trip, upsert, FK/CHECK/UNIQUE enforcement, transaction rollback. tests 122 passed; tools/check.ps1 CHECK GREEN

implementation_log.summary: Migration 0002_provenance: derived_from table (entity to source entity, role, optional Locator JSON, activity_id); triggers so that every insert or update of scan, blob, path_observation, archive_member, blob_classification, blob_relation, change_event and derived_from requires an existing RUNNING activity (enforced even for raw SQL); activities must be inserted as running and finish once; finished activities and identity columns are immutable; activities and links are never deleted. ProvenanceStore API: start_activity and finish_activity (params_hash per NFR-04), an activity() context manager (succeeded, failed or cancelled; notes keep only the exception class so no paths leak), link(), record_derived() (entity plus >=1 derived_from atomically; refuses empty or mismatched links), derived_from(), and the integrity queries pv1_violations(table, id) and unresolved_locators() for sbr doctor. transaction() nests via SAVEPOINTs. Knowledge-entity tables (P4/P5) register with pv1_violations when they arrive.

implementation_log.summary: src/sbr/jobs package: JobQueue over the existing work_item/work_output tables (migration 0004, already committed). enqueue() is idempotent on the (subject_id, stage, stage_version) unique key, so a re-run or a restarted pipeline never creates a duplicate row; bumping stage_version inserts a new row and leaves other subjects' rows untouched (exactly-affected re-enqueue). lease() atomically claims pending-and-due items or leased items whose lease has expired (a crashed worker's items) ordered by priority then age; an expired lease that already exhausted max_attempts is retired straight to 'failed' instead of being re-leased, so a crashed worker can never keep a poison item cycling. extend()/complete()/fail() all require the current lease_token, so a re-leased item's original (crashed) holder can never complete or fail it a second time. complete() writes the work_output artifact manifest and the work_item state transition in one SQLite transaction (atomic completion). fail() applies exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, ... capped at 15min) below max_attempts, else terminal 'failed'. jobs/dag.py: ready_stages() plus JobQueue.advance() enqueue exactly the downstream stages of a static stage DAG whose prerequisites are done at their current version (stage DAG enqueueing), idempotently. Schemas: WorkItem/WorkItemState/WorkOutput in schemas/operations.py (JobId/ManifestId in schemas/base.py), registered in db/registry.py as WORK_ITEM/WORK_OUTPUT TableSpecs, exported to schemas/WorkItem.json and schemas/WorkOutput.json.
implementation_log.verification: TS-QUEUE crash-resume test with an injectable millisecond clock (no real sleep, no subprocess): worker A leases an item and is never called again (simulated kill); a fresh JobQueue instance (worker B, as a restarted process would open) cannot claim it before the lease expires, claims it exactly once after, and worker A's stale lease_token can no longer complete it. Stage-version bump re-enqueues only the affected subject (the other subject's row is untouched). Backoff schedule and the max-attempts terminal transition verified; poison items confirmed never returned by lease() again, including via the expired-lease-reap path. Stage DAG advance() verified idempotent and correctly gated on prerequisite completion at the right version. 12/12 new tests passed; full suite 146 passed, 3 pre-existing Windows-only sourcefs/runtime-guard failures (this container is Linux, not Windows/WSL, so a `Regelungstechnik\\skript.pdf`-style os_path literal never resolves here; unrelated to this task, present before it). ruff and mypy clean on every file touched (both had pre-existing, unrelated debt in tools/validate_plan.py and tools/audit_crossrefs.py, and one pre-existing unused-ignore in tests/test_schemas.py:220 predating this session). tools/export_schemas.py --check clean. tools/validate_plan.py: PLAN CONSISTENT. tools/audit_crossrefs.py: CROSSREFS CLEAN.

implementation_log.summary: src/sbr/jobs/governor.py: ResourceGovernor.check(stage, active_workers=, active_in_stage=) is pure admission control — it answers 'may a worker for this stage (keep) run(ning) right now', ordered time-window, disk-floor, RAM-ceiling, worker-pool, per-stage-concurrency, and never touches work_item rows itself; the caller (pipeline runner) owns its own in-flight counts and passes them in. Metrics come through an injectable MetricsProvider (SystemMetrics: disk_free_gb, ram_used_gb, now), so the decision logic is unit-tested against simulated values (real_metrics() uses stdlib shutil.disk_usage for disk and resource.getrusage for RAM, no new third-party dependency added without a spike). time_windows (already validated in config.GovernorConfig as 'HH:MM-HH:MM') support windows that wrap past midnight. set_process_priority() sets the Windows process priority class via ctypes (IDLE/BELOW_NORMAL/NORMAL) and is a documented no-op (returns False) on platforms without ctypes.windll, matching the acceptance criterion that priority is set on Windows specifically.
implementation_log.verification: Unit tests with simulated SystemMetrics (no real disk/RAM probing, no real Windows API call): queue pauses exactly at the disk floor (inclusive boundary verified both sides); RAM ceiling pause; worker-pool count respected at the exact configured max; per-stage concurrency independent of the pool-wide limit; time windows admit inside and refuse outside, including a window that wraps past midnight, and an empty time_windows list always admits; when several limits are breached at once a reason is still returned (most-urgent-first ordering). set_process_priority() verified against a monkeypatched fake ctypes.windll.kernel32 (asserts SetPriorityClass is called with BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS) and verified to return False (no-op) when ctypes.windll is absent, as it is on this Linux container. 12/12 new tests passed; full suite 158 passed, the same 3 pre-existing Windows-only sourcefs/runtime-guard failures as before (unrelated to this task). ruff and mypy clean on every file touched. tools/export_schemas.py --check clean (no schema change this task). tools/validate_plan.py: PLAN CONSISTENT. tools/audit_crossrefs.py: CROSSREFS CLEAN.

implementation_log.summary: src/sbr/curation.py: schemas, loader and validation for the 7 curation/*.yaml files (ADR-029, HC-12): TaxonomyConcept, CourseMapEntry, CanonicalOverride, Exclusion, SensitivityOverride, ConceptCurationEntry, Approval, each a closed-world CurationModel (extra='forbid', frozen, but not StrictModel's strict=True -- YAML values are not already fully typed the way validate_json's input is). load_curation_file() parses with ruamel.yaml in round-trip mode (typ='rt': preserves comments, key order and quoting style) and validates every record; a syntax error carries ruamel's own line/column message, and a schema-validation error looks up the failing entry's source line from ruamel's CommentedMap line-tracking (.lc.line) -- both surface as CurationError naming the file and line, never a bare traceback. New dependency: ruamel.yaml>=0.18 (a narrow, uncontroversial YAML serialization library, not a docs/34-gated technology choice; no spike needed, same footing as the project's existing blake3/xxhash/typer/pydantic dependencies). append_approval() is the only write path for approvals.yaml (the one append-only file): it loads the existing document with ruamel (so untouched entries' comments survive), appends the new entry, verifies every previously-recorded entry is still present as an exact prefix before writing, and refuses a duplicate approval_id or a file that is not the bare list it is defined as. Seeded curation/*.yaml (taxonomy, course_map, canonical_overrides, exclusions, sensitivity_overrides, concept_curation, approvals), each an empty, valid, header-commented file; later tasks (T-P4-14/15 etc.) populate them.
implementation_log.verification: All 7 seeded curation/*.yaml files load cleanly with zero records via their dedicated loader functions. Each schema round-trips real content (bilingual taxonomy edges; mixed-case owner folder abbreviations in course_map, which schemas.base.Slug would have rejected -- a local, looser CurationId pattern is used instead; exclusion/sensitivity-override path vs blob scopes; concept rename actions). Rejection verified for: syntactically invalid YAML (line number present), a missing required field on one entry among several (names the failing entry index and its line), an unknown/extra field, a non-mapping top-level document, a missing file, and a bare-list file that is not a list. A plain read never rewrites the file (comments untouched). append_approval() verified to: create the file if absent; preserve an existing entry's comment when appending a second entry; refuse (and leave the file unchanged for) a duplicate approval_id; refuse a non-list approvals file. 17/17 new tests passed; full suite 183 passed, the same 3 pre-existing Windows-only sourcefs/runtime-guard failures as before (unrelated to this task). ruff and mypy clean on every file touched. detect-secrets scan of all new/changed files: no findings. tools/export_schemas.py --check clean (no sbr.schemas change this task -- curation records are a separate, hand-edited-file schema family, not registry/knowledge-DB records). tools/validate_plan.py: PLAN CONSISTENT.

implementation_log.summary: tests/fixtures/generate.py: deterministic synthetic fixture corpus generator (docs/33 §3), no copyrighted corpus content. generate(root) builds tests/fixtures/corpus/: skript.pdf (pdflatex-compiled, two real equations, with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH + \pdftrailerid{} for byte-reproducible output), uebung1.docx and folien.pptx (each with a genuine m:oMath/a14:m OMML equation tree, not plain text -- DOCX via a body-level m:oMathPara, PPTX via the mc:AlternateContent/a14:m DrawingML extension with a text fallback), scan_seite1.pdf (Pillow-rendered, image-only, no text layer -- a simulated scan), skript_annotiert.pdf (skript.pdf plus one real pypdf FreeText annotation object), archiv.zip (a legacy CP437-encoded, non-UTF-8-flagged entry name with an umlaut, via a custom ZipInfo subclass overriding _encodeFilenameFlags -- Python's zipfile only ever writes ASCII or UTF-8-flagged names by default, never true CP437, so this reproduces what pre-UTF-8 DOS-era zip tools actually wrote; plus an embedded exact duplicate of skript.pdf), Formelsammlung/skript_kopie.pdf (an exact-duplicate file, ADR-031), and an 'Ubung' (umlaut) path component throughout. Every embedded timestamp/id/metadata field (LaTeX's PDF /ID, docx/pptx core properties AND their own zip container's per-entry mtimes, which python-docx/pptx set to 'now' unless the container is re-zipped with fixed entries, the scanned PDF's /CreationDate, the annotated PDF's writer /ID) is pinned, so two runs -- even a real wall-clock second apart -- produce byte-identical output. 'Moved files' is deliberately not a second baked tree: a P2 test builds that scenario itself by relocating a generated file between two scans; the interesting part is the move, not the corpus. New dev-only dependencies (never imported by src/sbr): python-docx, python-pptx, pillow, pypdf, lxml-stubs -- narrow, uncontroversial fixture-authoring libraries, not docs/34-gated technology choices. New system tool: TeX Live (texlive-latex-base/-recommended, texlive-fonts-recommended) is needed only to *regenerate* the corpus, never to run the test suite, since the generated tree is committed to git (synthetic, so safe to commit per docs/33 §3).
implementation_log.verification: Cross-run determinism verified with a real >1s wall-clock gap between two generations into separate directories: every file's BLAKE3 hash (sbr.ids.hash_bytes) matches. Re-running into the same directory is idempotent, and the committed tests/fixtures/corpus/ matches a fresh generation exactly (not stale). Content sanity verified for every advertised scenario: the LaTeX PDF's extracted text contains the real compiled equations; the DOCX and PPTX open validly via python-docx/python-pptx and their raw XML contains a real m:oMath / a14:m tree; the scanned PDF extracts zero text; the annotated PDF carries exactly one /Annots entry; the archive's umlaut-bearing entry name has no UTF-8 flag bit set (genuine CP437) and its embedded 'duplicate' member hashes identically to the real skript.pdf; the Formelsammlung copy hashes identically to the original; the umlaut path component exists; generate() replaces (never merges into) a pre-existing output directory. 12/12 new tests passed; full suite 195 passed, the same 3 pre-existing Windows-only sourcefs/runtime-guard failures as before (unrelated to this task). ruff (check and format) and mypy clean on every file touched (lxml-stubs added for lxml's types); the two pre-existing mypy unused-ignore findings (tests/test_schemas.py:220, tests/safety/test_sourcefs.py:54) and tools/validate_plan.py's pre-existing lint debt are untouched and confirmed to predate this session. detect-secrets scan of every new/changed file, including the generated binary fixtures: no findings. tools/export_schemas.py --check clean (no sbr.schemas change this task). tools/validate_plan.py: PLAN CONSISTENT. tools/audit_crossrefs.py: CROSSREFS CLEAN.
